Fusebox now has a native iPhone app, with notifications through a push relay that any self-hosted server can use. Dead sign-ins, capacity limits and keys that are out of credit are handled the way the providers now behave. Faults can be dismissed, ChatGPT subscriptions show when they renew, and the Usage page shows which Claude Code entrypoint each call came from.

## Changes

- **iPhone app.** A SwiftUI app for a Fusebox server, under `ios/`. It shows:
  - each subscription's meters with the even-pace mark;
  - the combined weekly limits and the faults;
  - accounts with their actions;
  - the request log with its routing explanation;
  - usage charts;
  - home-screen widgets.

  It follows the dashboard's design and works on the iPhone Duo's outer and unfolded screens. It is in TestFlight and in App Review for the App Store.
- **Push relay.** Apple delivers the app's notifications only through a holder of its push key, so `fusebox push-relay` runs a small relay that holds it.
  - Fusebox seals each notification with AES-256-GCM for the device. It sends only a random handle and the ciphertext, so neither the relay nor Apple can read a notification, and Fusebox never learns the device token.
  - The new `push-relay` setting defaults to `https://push.whombat.com`; `""` turns the relay off.
  - A server with its own key can send to the app through APNs directly, using the new `apns` section.
- **Dead sign-ins.** A refresh token the provider refuses for good is asked once, not every minute until someone signs in again. That covers `invalid_grant`, revoked, expired, reused or invalidated tokens, and a bare 401 from OpenAI's token endpoint.
  - The account keeps serving while its access token lasts, then sits out, as a switched-off account does, until a sign-in. A newer token found in its file also brings it back.
  - It says "Sign-in expired" on the dashboard and in notifications, and the hold survives restarts.
  - `invalid_client` backs off instead of holding the account out.
  - `/readyz`, `/metrics` and the overview no longer count held accounts as ready.
- **Codex capacity limits.** OpenAI's `turn_rate_limit_exceeded` ("Codex is at capacity") is an overload, not the account's rate limit.
  - A long wait moves the request to the next account at once, and pauses no model.
  - With no account left, the wait goes to the client as `Retry-After` (at most ten minutes), also from inside a stream and over WebSocket, so Codex waits out that turn instead of ending it.
- **When every account is sitting out.** A short rate limit, used-up limit or quota check (a minute or less) is sent as `Retry-After`. A longer one gets no header, so clients don't sleep through it, and OpenAI clients get `usage_limit_reached` with `resets_at` instead. A sign-in or permission problem is never offered as a wait.
- **Out of credit.** An Anthropic API key whose credit ran out ("Your credit balance is too low") sits out for 30 minutes and requests move on. Meanwhile a request with no other account left gets that 400 again, also after a restart. The dashboard, notifications and the app say "API credit used up".
- **Requests refused as sent.** ChatGPT's 502 "response protection is unavailable" is answered at once, without retries on this account or another.
- **Meta.** Muse Code's `client_attestation_denied` rejects the request, not the account: no new key, no pause and no account error. Meta's accounts are skipped for the whole request.
- **Remote compaction.** Codex's remote compaction leaves Kimi and Meta accounts out, since they can't compact. If only they serve the model, the request gets a 400 explaining how to make Codex compact locally.
- **Private events.** Codex's private Responses events (`response.metadata`, `codex.*`) and Meta's usage telemetry reach Codex clients only, including app-server hosts such as T3 Code. Strict clients no longer fail on them. `/metrics` counts what was left out.
- **WebSocket.**
  - Error events carry string codes and any wait, as Codex reads them.
  - A rate limit or capacity error that arrives before anything else moves the turn to HTTP when another account can take it.
- **Faults can be dismissed** from the dashboard and the app. A dismissal is kept on the server until the fault clears or a warning becomes an error.
- **Subscription renewals.** ChatGPT accounts show when they renew or end, and a reminder arrives two days before (`notifications.renewals`, on by default). Claude gives no billing date, so its accounts show none.
- **Claude Code entrypoints.** The Usage page shows each day's share of calls from the Agent SDK (`sdk-ts`, `sdk-cli`), as against the CLI and others. A new Entrypoint tab in the breakdown filters the page.
- **Dashboard.**
  - Meters show quota left by default.
  - The combined weekly row reads like an account's weekly meter, with the forecast's status beside it.
- **Translation fixes.**
  - Prefill is dropped for Claude models that reject it.
  - Claude Code's mid-conversation tool additions become callable tools for GPT models.
  - Empty Gemini system parts are removed.
  - Vertex `us`/`eu` use Google's regional hosts.
  - Antigravity Opus and Sonnet 5.5 get structured-output schemas as instructions.
  - Schema placeholders and numeric limits are fixed for Gemini.
  - A Gemini turn without a role that calls a function counts as the model's.
  - Devin `(level-fast)` efforts reach Devin's fast models.
  - Translated prompt overflows say `context_length_exceeded`.
- **Robustness.**
  - An unreadable auth directory keeps its accounts.
  - A sign-in whose file name another account holds gets a name of its own.
  - API-key switches survive restarts.
  - Upstream 504s from media work aren't retried elsewhere.
  - The no-5-hour finding survives restarts.
  - Named-client spend is read through the time index (5 s to 0.01 s on a large database).
  - CORS lets browser apps send `Authorization`.

## Upgrading

- **Database and state files.** The usage database stays on schema 5; the first start adds the entrypoint side tables. `.cooldowns.state` gains optional fields, which v0.12.1 ignores, so going back is safe.
- **New settings:** `push-relay` (default `https://push.whombat.com`), `notifications.renewals` (on), and an optional `apns` section. Nothing else changes in `config.yaml`.
- **New routes:**
  - `POST /api/push/apns`;
  - `POST /api/faults/dismiss` and `/api/faults/restore`, `GET /api/faults/dismissed`;
  - `GET /api/usage/entrypoints`.
- **API changes:**
  - `/api/overview` adds `accounts.signin`.
  - Route steps can be `signin`.
  - Cooldown kinds can be `credit`.
- **If an account says "Sign-in expired",** sign in again; Fusebox no longer keeps retrying its refused token.

Validation passed 897 Rust, 171 dashboard and 58 iPhone app tests, with CI on Linux, macOS and Windows. Production has run this code since 3 November 2026. The research and action list behind the provider fixes are in [notes/cliproxyapi-research-2026-11-03.md](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.13.0/notes/cliproxyapi-research-2026-11-03.md) and [notes/cliproxyapi-action-list-2026-11-03.md](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.13.0/notes/cliproxyapi-action-list-2026-11-03.md).
